figures.caption: Table 1 The requirements and challenges of surface coatings for cathode materials. Requirements Challenges Thin coating layer Inhomogeneous coating, Island coating, Bare (uncoated) regions Ionic & electronic conducting layer Increase in charge transfer resistance ( R ct ), poor ionic and electronic conductivity Stable upon cycling Formation of cracks due to fatigue, delamination Easy processing Change of cathode surface chemistry in complicated wet processing (wet coating) Cheaper coating materials Expensive coating precursor, increase cathode material cost

figures.caption: Table 2 Comparison of advantages and disadvantages of various coating processes. Process Advantages Disadvantages Wet chemical coating Simple, economical, commercially viable Thickness, morphology, and homogeneity are quite diﬃcult to control. The extra cost is involved in wastewater treatment and powder drying. Compatibility of grinding media, solvent, cathode, and coating materials Atomic layer deposition (ALD) Nano coating, uniform coating, precise control over coating composition Expensive, commercially not viable Dry coating (Ball milling) Simple, cheap and commercially viable (scalable) Thickness, morphology, and homogeneity are quite diﬃcult to control, leads to non-uniform coating Hydrothermal Uniform coating Expensive, sophisticated, commercially not viable Chemical vapor deposition (CVD) Uniform coating, thickness easy to control Expensive, commercially not viable
